correctness.rationale: Analytically check all Fourier and radial Laplacian blocks, positive-semidefinite unit-gap inequalities, and the Rayleigh concavity averaging over graph automorphisms. The residual cost minimization is a one-dimensional strictly convex function with a unique root for every \(0<t<\delta\); at/above delta, \(c=2\) minimizes c+g(c) and gives a continuum/unique symmetric optimizer respectively. Homogeneity yields the unrestricted optimal value. Standalone verify.py passes 1180 actual exact-symbolic and numerical checks, not taken as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The full-text fundamental Sun et al. treatment gives the general optimization problem without this helm price threshold. Jafarizadeh 2015 supplies the rim-deleted symmetric star as a covered boundary but not the complementary rim-positive regime nor the precise condition for deleting optional cycle edges. Discrete-time helm SLEM is a different optimization problem; alias and parameter literature searches did not find a covering priced-helm continuous-time theorem. Unindexed equivalences remain possible.
residual_risks: A fully equivalent specialization could exist in unindexed or inaccessible weighted-helm consensus literature.

value.rationale: The complete sharp price/support classification for a natural family of 2n+1-state hub-cycle-leaf networks includes a nontrivial transition t=2(1-cos(2pi/n)), an exactly flat critical optimizer face, and a dimension phase n=5/6/7 under equal prices. It tells a network designer when the entire cycle may be replaced by zero-cost zero-conductance links while retaining the exact optimal continuous-time mixing rate. This is not just a restatement of the known zero-cycle symmetric-star calculation, nor a numerical finite-instance exercise.
